key_insight: A physics-grounded digital-twin prototype combines weld-pool simulation, AI surrogates and robotic control to screen in-space welding strategies before experimental testing.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could support adaptive welding control for on-orbit assembly and repair, but performance remains simulation-based.
method: Finite-volume thermal model with phase change, effective thermocapillary transport and local pressure; gravity assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates evaluated using repeated five-fold cross-validation.
Simulated UR5 seam tracking with proportional adjustment of the welding power-source setting.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs; finite-volume re-evaluation placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop operating points within an illustrative 1–3 mm root-side-width band.
watch_item: Thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity and robotic hardware-in-the-loop validation are still needed; gravity does not enter the thermal energy equation.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
